I'm Not firearm savy, What's dry holding?

Just like it sounds, Holding on target and doing nothing else which develops that one skill. It's amazing what you notice while doing that when you're NOT thinking about squeezing a trigger, dealing with recoil, or anxious about shot placement. I suppose if you only ever shoot prone, off a bipod, this is a moot point but that'd be a stupid pigeonhole to put yourself in if you were prepping for worst case scenarios. Same is true for dry-firing, you don't hold on anything (just be in proper position for the given firearm, pistols are the easiest) and work the trigger. I'd usually close my eyes and just picture myself shooting (in a match at the Olympic Training Center in Colorado Springs) while focusing on the trigger. Then combine the 2, if you're Really watching the sights you can see jerks of the finger, flinching, etc... all the things that typically plague shooters. The best shooters I know spend 80% of their time doing these 2 things.

As with most things, shooting is Easily 80% mental. You can develop those skills without ever firing a shot, but it's more dull than watching paint dry or grass grow, you HAVE to have motivation. That's why I live-fire, it's a personal reward for training. Plus, you DO need live-fire in the overall picture because recoil is a real thing that you much become accustom to as well. So is the noise, and mostly the anticipation of both.
